I'm preparing a kickoff for engineering and design leads on adding team workspaces to a B2B note-taking app. Below is the brief for a product requirements document (PRD) they will read at the kickoff. Please draft the PRD from it.

<brief>
Product: a B2B note-taking app.
Feature: team workspaces.
Audience: engineering and design leads, reading the PRD at the kickoff for this feature.

Problem: I have no evidence yet (no data, no customer quotes). State the problem in one line from the request, and in the Problem section add a clearly marked "Evidence gap" note saying that evidence still needs to be gathered. Do not invent statistics, customer quotes, research findings, or competitor facts.

In scope for v1:
- Creating a workspace
- Inviting members by email
- Shared notes
- Two roles only: admin and member

Out of scope (list exactly these three): billing changes, SSO, guest access.

Open question to leave open: what happens to existing shared notes (migration). List it under Open questions with no recommended answer. Do not resolve it, and do not write requirements that assume an answer.

Success metric: 20% of paid accounts create a workspace within 60 days. Use the figure exactly as written.
</brief>

Use these sections, in this order: Overview, Problem, Goals and non-goals, User stories, Requirements, Success metrics, Open questions. Make it at most about 2 pages. Write requirements that engineers and designers can act on, as numbered, testable statements covering only the in-scope items. Build only the features listed. If a requirement needs a detail the brief doesn't give, write it as an open question or mark it "Assumption" instead of deciding it quietly. Label any number you propose beyond the stated metric as "Proposed".

Reply with the PRD only, then a short list headed "Assumptions I made" naming anything you assumed, or "None" if there were none. Nothing follows that list.
